scope: Managed Linux headed-browser source and local component verification

tests.suite: Login state and pinned Linux browser lifecycle
Two real temporary Chromium processes with controlled launcher
Existing desktop, cancellation, pool, lifecycle and network
Python browser protocol and real loopback relay
Python desktop session and concurrent child cgroup cleanup

initialFailuresResolved: Real Chromium omitted an emptied localStorage origin; synchronization now recognizes deletion and preserves edits made after observation.
Independent review found session cleanup could race browser child-cgroup removal; both sides now handle only the verified empty child idempotently and still wait for descendants.
Local socket tests initially required sandbox network permission; reruns used only loopback synthetic fixtures.
limitations: Real Chromium tests use temporary headless macOS processes with a controlled launcher; they do not prove Linux namespace or headed-display behavior.
Linux requires fixed root-installed full Chromium, dynamic dependencies, user namespaces, cgroup v2 kill and a valid existing desktop session.
Existing total 768 MiB, per-screen 384 MiB and 64-process limits were not changed.
Only unpartitioned HTTP(S) cookies and localStorage are synchronized; IndexedDB, sessionStorage, partitioned cookies, passkeys and password managers remain separate.
